subject: SIG/CAIQ: retention carve-out and ephemeral KV cache - NeuroLink
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@neurolink.com>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: security@neurolink.com
Date: 2028-02-08T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: SIG/CAIQ follow-up - retention carve-out questions

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the SIG and CAIQ files you shared last week. Our security team dug into section A.3 (data lifecycle) and has a couple of specific questions before we close the compliance review:

1) Ephemeral KV cache: the SIG response indicates an ephemeral cache exists for model context / KV. Can you confirm the default retention for KV cache state (in hours)? Does any copy persist in durable logs or S3 after eviction?

2) Debug traces / request logs: we need an explicit statement of maximum retention for request/response traces for tenant-scoped debugging. Is 30 days the maximum across all deployments? Are there customer-specific exceptions?

3) Forensics hold: our legal team has asked whether Redwood can support a customer-specific 180-day preservation window for a single tenant (NeuroLink) for investigatory reasons. If so, what mechanisms and evidence artifacts (CAIQ/SIG artifacts, proof-of-delete process, keystore handback) would you provide?

Please see attached PDF with annotated questions (NeuroLink-SIG-questions.pdf). If easier, we can jump on a 30-minute call. Goal is to finish the SIG QA by 02/12.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Mercer
Director, Information Security
NeuroLink Therapeutics
[attachment: NeuroLink-SIG-questions.pdf (PDF)]

From: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Alex.Mercer@neurolink.com
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-02-08T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ follow-up - retention carve-out questions

Alex —

Appreciate the clear write-up and the annotated PDF. Short answers up front, followed by details below:

- Ephemeral KV cache: default TTL is 24 hours. Cache contents are in-memory on the serving nodes and are not written to persistent object storage under normal operation. We do persist compact debug snapshots in our debug pipeline only when tenant-level debug is enabled (see below).

- Debug traces / request logs: standard request/response traces are retained for a default of 30 days in our telemetry tier. Customers can opt into extended retention via a contractual add-on or Dedicated/Private deployment where retention controls are configurable.

- 180-day forensics hold: yes — we can support a tenant-scoped 180-day preservation via one of two patterns: (1) Reserved evidence escrow (periodic export and secure handoff to customer-managed storage), or (2) Private deployment with delegated retention policy and keystore-handback. For hosted customers we typically provide an "escrow snapshot" deliverable plus signed proof-of-delete artifacts at the end of the hold.

Attachments: I’m attaching a concise retention matrix and a CAIQ slice that points to the SOC2 artifact IDs you can reference (Redwood-SIG-CAIQ-Retention-Matrix.pdf, CAIQ-evidence-slice.xlsx).

Technical details (abridged):
- KV cache lifecycle: cache entries generated per-inference; eviction policy LRU; TTL = 24h by default; no write-through to S3. When debug_snapshot=true (admin flag), we capture a deterministic, pseudonymized snapshot to a secured bucket for up to X days (configurable).
- Request logs: two tiers — (a) telemetry traces (30d default), (b) forensic snapshots (customer opt-in). Telemetry retention cannot exceed the tenant contract if on Hosted.
- Evidence & attestation: we can deliver checksumed export bundles, signed deletion manifests, and CAIQ reference IDs. For a 180-day hold we propose an initial export plus monthly immutability manifests.

Next step: Markus — can you confirm feasibility, delivery timeline for an escrow export + deletion manifest if we commit to a forensics hold by 02/15? Irene — any additional SOC2/CAIQ artifact ids we should include for NeuroLink?

- Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security Programs, Redwood Inference
[attachment: Redwood-SIG-CAIQ-Retention-Matrix.pdf (PDF)]

From: markus.klein@redwood.ai
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-02-08T12:45:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: NeuroLink 180-day retention - implementation options

Neha / Irene —

Quick internal note on options and constraints:

1) Hosted escrow snapshot (low lift): we can export tenant-scoped debug artifacts daily into a gated S3 bucket, apply server-side encryption with a dedicated envelope key, and hand over access to NeuroLink or their retained escrow provider. Deliverables = monthly export + checksum manifest + signed deletion cert after retention expires. Risk = additional storage costs and operational runbook for secure transfer. Estimated delivery: 2 weeks to stand up the pipeline + 1 week of validation.

2) Pseudonymized snapshot (medium lift): generate a snapshot with PII redaction/pseudonymization before export. This reduces privacy risk but increases engineering validation (we need to ensure no reidentification vectors remain). Estimated delivery: 4–6 weeks.

3) Private deployment (highest assurance): we push a Private tile for NeuroLink (customer-managed network/KMS), they control retention via config. More procurement/sales effort; typical timeline 8–12 weeks.

Commercial: supporting a hosted 180-day escrow should be scoped as a one-time professional-services engagement with a small monthly storage fee. Recommend proposing PS work order and $Xk month.

Irene — once you confirm which CAIQ artifact IDs to include, I’ll draft the technical appendix for the export format and evidence manifests.

-Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Customer Reliability
[internal-only]

From: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Alex.Mercer@neurolink.com, security@neurolink.com
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-02-09T15:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ follow-up - retention carve-out questions

Alex —

Thanks for the patience. We discussed options internally and can support NeuroLink’s requested 180-day tenant-scoped preservation via our hosted escrow snapshot pattern (option 1). Summary of commitments and artifacts:

- Retention mechanism: daily tenant-scoped export to a secure, access-controlled S3 escrow bucket (encrypted with Redwood envelope key) retained 180 days.
- Deliverables: monthly export bundles (tar.gz) with SHA256 manifest, a signed deletion certificate at hold expiry, and CAIQ/SIG artifact references (see attached CAIQ slice).
- Evidence: Redwood will supply the CAIQ reference IDs and SOC2 artifact pointers verifying the export process, plus a sample proof-of-delete workflow. Irene has appended the exact SOC2 artifact IDs in the attached sheet.
- Privacy controls: exports will exclude raw PII by default; we can provide a pseudonymized variant on request (additional validation required).
- Cost & timeline: we can stand up the escrow pipeline in ~3 weeks after PO and SOW; estimated one-time PS of $7,500 and $120/month storage estimate (approx). Final commercials subject to procurement review.

Action items for NeuroLink:
- Confirm acceptance of the escrow approach by 02/15.
- If you require pseudonymization, indicate scope (fields to redact) so we can size the validation work.
- Suggested meeting: Wed 02/10 10:00am PT to walk artifacts.

I’ve attached the retention matrix and CAIQ slice as promised. If accepted, I’ll follow up with a draft SOW and evidence appendix.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security Programs | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142
